rationale: Positives: The agent verified identity correctly using full name + zip, sought explicit confirmation before attempting to change the order, and referenced the original PayPal method for any refund. Negatives: (1) The agent asserted the order was pending without tool evidence, violating the "don’t invent missing facts" rule. (2) The agent failed to complete the requested partial cancellation; multiple modify tool attempts errored and the agent didn’t provide a workable alternative within policy/tools (e.g., check for a supported partial-cancel flow or compute/communicate a refund total). (3) When partial changes proved impossible, the user asked to change the default address to the Seattle address shown in the order. The agent refused unless the user re-typed the address, even though the verified order clearly contained the full Seattle address and policy allows acting on the authenticated user’s data after stating the exact change and obtaining confirmation. The agent neither proposed the exact Seattle address from the order for confirmation nor executed the update. (4) No final, correct information (e.g., refund total) was provided. Because the user’s requests were not completed and there was an unsupported claim about order status, this does not meet the pass bar.
